To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the basis of the unresponsiveness induced by BCG infection is a lack of IL-2 production rather than a lack in reactive T cells.

the basis of mycobacterial immunosuppression is a deficiency in IL-2 production and that the reversal of BCG immunosuppression by IL-2 is a result of a restoration of the IL-2-dependent proliferative capacity of T lymphocytes.

BCG-infected, immunosuppressed mice were able to produce IL-2 spontaneously and to respond to PPD in vitro when their T cells were cultured with IL-2, and that in vivo administration of IL-2 reversed BCG-induced immunodepression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new therapeutic approach for the treatment of BCG-induced tuberculosis.
the use of recombinant IL-2 to restore the immune system of BCG-immunosensitized mice.
the development and evaluation of an in vivo immunomodulator based on the administration of a preparation containing IL-2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the immunosuppression observed in BCG-infected animals can be reversed in vivo and in vitro by the administration of IL-2-containing preparations.
IL-2 is a potent immunopotentiator and that its use could be a useful therapeutic modality in the management of patients with tuberculosis.
IL-2 is a major mediator in BCG-induced immunoprotection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BCG infection in mice induces a state of unresponsivness which is reversed in vitro and in vio by the administration of IL-2-containing preparations.
BCG infection induces a state of immunosuppression that is characterized by a lack of IL-2 production.
the administration of IL-2-containing preparations to mice infected with BCG can reverse the immunosuppression associated with this infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL-2 is a potent stimulator for the recovery of T-cell unresponsivness in vivo and in vitro in BCG-infected animals.
IL-2 is an important mediator of the host response to mycobacterial infection.
IL-2 is a potent immunoregulator that can reverse the immunosuppressive effects of BCG.
